page.title: Groceries
page.purpose: Turn an explicit plan and inventory policy into an honest shopping list with stock considered, package plans, separated unknown costs, and a distinct purchase confirmation.

priorities.statement: The plan or date range the list was derived from is stated before any line.
A shopping checkmark is checklist state only and is never presented as a purchase, stock change, or consumption.
Quantity needed, stock considered, amount missing, package plan, and price each show their own unknown state.
The checkout summary separates priced packages from unpriced items and from unmodeled costs such as tax or delivery.
Explicitly adding purchases to the pantry previews idempotent quantity and price changes before any stock write.

states.description: The surface at rest with data present; the state a journey step assumes when it names none.
First read of the page's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
The read succeeded and there is genuinely nothing, which is distinct from not-yet-loaded.
Some contributing data could not be read; what is missing is named rather than shown as zero.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
The request failed; the reason and the next available action are stated.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified next to it.
A write is in flight; the affected control says why it is unavailable.
The client cannot reach the API; read-only or queued behavior is explained.
One or more package prices are missing; the checkout reads as a known subtotal plus a count of unpriced items.
On-hand or asserted stock reduces the amount to buy without making consumed food economically free.
The explicit 'Add purchases to pantry' preview is open with quantities, packages, prices, and partial-fulfillment options.

elements.description: The explicit plan or date range the list was derived from, such as 'For your meals, September 21-27.'
Checked and remaining counts, labeled so a check is not read as bought.

elements.name: Shopping list
elements.description: Derived lines grouped practically, each with need, stock, missing, package, and price.
Total planned need for the line in a compatible unit.
Stock considered, with its confidence state and last-updated origin.
Amount missing after usable stock is considered.
Selected package plan and package count, which may be unknown even when the needed mass is known.
Estimated price with its observation date and conditions.
States which of amount, conversion, package size, or price is unknown for a line.

elements.name: Already have
elements.description: Creates a stock assertion with its own basis, stronger than a shopping checkmark.

elements.name: Add a manual item
elements.description: Adds a manual grocery item that replanning cannot delete.
Known package subtotal with unpriced and unmodeled costs kept separate.
The count of items without a usable price.
Names tax, delivery, travel, or membership conditions that are not modeled.

elements.name: Add purchases to pantry
elements.description: Opens the explicit purchase preview; checking a box alone never triggers it.

elements.name: Add purchases to pantry
elements.description: Previews quantities and prices and supports partial fulfillment before an idempotent write.
The stock and spend changes the confirmation would create.
Flags an overridden purchase quantity whose plan need has since changed.

claims.statement: The shopping list states the plan or date range it was derived from before any line.
Checking a line is presented as checklist state only, and adding to the pantry is a separate explicit confirmation.
The checkout reports a known subtotal plus a count of unpriced items and never titles an incomplete subtotal as a total.
A line can show a known needed amount with an unknown package count, and the unknown part is named rather than filled in.
Stock considered is shown separately from the amount missing, with its confidence state and origin.
Adding purchases previews the quantity and price changes and supports partial fulfillment before an idempotent stock write.
Manual grocery items remain distinct from plan-derived requirements and are not deleted by replanning.
An overridden purchase quantity is retained and carries a mismatch badge when the plan need later changes.
The 'Already have' action creates a stock assertion with its own basis rather than a bare checklist mark.
The shopping list never scrolls the whole document sideways; each line wraps or scrolls within its own region.
